heading: Matrix product unitaries: structure, index and symmetry phases, after Cirac, Pérez-García, Schuch and Verstraete
lede: A matrix product unitary is a translation-invariant tensor network whose periodic contraction is a unitary operator on every ring. In 2017 Cirac, Pérez-García, Schuch and Verstraete showed that, after blocking finitely many sites, every such operator is a two-layer circuit of local unitaries followed by a shift, that two tensors give the same unitaries exactly when their local gates differ by unitaries on the internal legs, and that an index, half the base-two logarithm of the ratio of two ranks, measures the flow of information along the chain and classifies these operators up to continuous deformation and the addition of trivial ancillas. They then classified matrix product unitaries invariant under complex conjugation, time reversal and transposition. In Lean the structure theorem, the standard form, the fundamental theorem (in the form that compares tensors on rings of even length, since the printed all-length converse fails), the index with its blocking, product and continuity properties, and the local characterizations of the symmetries for canonical standard forms are proved. The complete index theorem, the continuous choice of standard forms and the symmetry phase classifications remain open.
description: Progress of the Lean 4 formalization of matrix product unitaries after Cirac, Pérez-García, Schuch and Verstraete, arXiv:1703.09188.

streamNames.6136: Canonical form II under products, transforms and paths

routes.heading: Structure, standard form and the fundamental theorem
routes.intro: A tensor with two physical legs and two virtual legs of dimension D generates, on a ring of N sites, an operator UN on (ℂd)⊗N. The tensor is a matrix product unitary when every UN is unitary. After blocking, the tensor can be taken simple: its two-site contraction factors through two isometries of ranks r and ℓ, with rℓ = d2. All results of this part are proved.

stages.title: Unitarity, normality and simple tensors
stages.physics: The transfer operator of a matrix product unitary has a unique eigenvalue of modulus one, so the tensor is normal; after blocking a bounded number of sites, the double layer of the tensor and its adjoint collapses to a rank-one contraction, which is the paper's simplicity condition.
stages.delivers: Normality of every matrix product unitary and the bounded blocking theorem for simplicity.

stages.title: Two ranks and the two-layer circuit
stages.physics: Cutting the two-site contraction of a simple tensor in two ways gives two singular value decompositions with ranks r and ℓ. Their factors assemble into two unitary gates u and v, and the operator on every ring is the circuit of u on even pairs followed by v on odd pairs: the standard form.
stages.delivers: The standard form, and the fundamental theorem comparing two simple tensors through their gates on rings of even length.

routes.heading: The index
routes.intro: The index of a matrix product unitary is ½ log2(r/ℓ) for the two ranks of a simple blocked tensor, the net quantum information moved to the right per site; it is a real number, the logarithm of a rational one. The paper shows that it does not depend on the blocking, adds under tensor products and composition, is constant along continuous paths, and characterizes the operator up to continuous deformation and the addition of trivial sites.

stages.title: Blocking, products and continuity
stages.physics: The ratio of the two ranks is unchanged by blocking and multiplies under tensor products and composition; the ranks are lower semicontinuous and their product is fixed, so both are constant along a path of matrix product unitaries.
stages.delivers: Well-definedness, additivity and continuity of the index.

stages.title: The index theorem and continuous standard forms
stages.physics: Two matrix product unitaries are equivalent, connected by a path after adding trivial sites, exactly when their indices agree. One direction is continuity; the other builds the path explicitly through standard forms, which requires choosing the gates continuously along a path.
stages.delivers: The four clauses of the index theorem and the continuous choice of standard form.

routes.heading: Symmetries and their phases
routes.intro: A matrix product unitary may be invariant under complex conjugation, time reversal (the adjoint) or transposition. For each symmetry the paper characterizes invariance by local equations on the gates, extracts discrete invariants, and classifies symmetric matrix product unitaries up to symmetry-preserving deformation.

stages.title: Symmetry-preserving equivalence
stages.physics: Two symmetric matrix product unitaries are equivalent under the symmetry when a path of symmetric operators joins them after adding symmetric trivial sites; the paper reduces this to a path of standard forms respecting the local symmetry equations.
stages.delivers: The standard-form path criterion for symmetric equivalence.

stages.title: Complex conjugation
stages.physics: Conjugation invariance holds exactly when the gates satisfy ū = (x ⊗ y)u and v̄ = v(y† ⊗ x†) for unitaries x, y that are both symmetric or both skew-symmetric. Normal forms of such matrices reduce the gates to orthogonal or symplectic ones, and the determinant and the symmetric or skew type give the phases.
stages.delivers: The local characterization, the orthogonal and symplectic normal forms of the gates, and the classification of conjugation-symmetric phases.

stages.title: Time reversal and transposition
stages.physics: Invariance under the adjoint on rings of even length holds exactly when, on four consecutive spins, (𝟙 ⊗ v23 ⊗ 𝟙)(u12 ⊗ u34) = σ(x12 ⊗ x34†)(𝟙 ⊗ v23† ⊗ 𝟙) for a unitary x on two spins and a sign σ = ±1; it forces r = ℓ = d. The sign is read off from a trace of the two-site operator, does not depend on the choices, is constant along symmetric paths, and behaves under blocking according to parity.
stages.delivers: The local characterizations, the sign σ with its trace formula, invariance and blocking parity, and its comparison with the sign of matrix product states.

routes.heading: Examples
routes.intro: The shift, the CZX operator and a model of a topological insulator illustrate the index and the symmetry phases.

stages.title: Shifts, CZX and topological insulators
stages.physics: The shift on sites of dimension d has index log2 d; families of shifts with swaps realize distinct symmetry phases, and the CZX operator realizes a nontrivial phase of a symmetry acting on two spins per site.
stages.delivers: Explicit tensors, their standard forms, indices and symmetry invariants.

glossary: A translation-invariant tensor whose periodic contraction on every ring of N sites is a unitary operator.
A tensor whose two-site double-layer contraction with its adjoint is rank one, reached from any matrix product unitary after blocking boundedly many sites.
The presentation of a simple matrix product unitary as a layer of gates u on even pairs followed by a layer of gates v on odd pairs.
½ log2(r/ℓ) for the two ranks of a simple tensor: the net information flow per site, a real number.
Two matrix product unitaries are equivalent when, after tensoring with trivial sites, a continuous path of matrix product unitaries joins them.
